correctness.rationale: All 24 edges are defined explicitly. A first-uncovered-vertex exhaustive matching recursion yields all 33 matchings and 20 unordered three-perfect-matching factorizations. Independent edge-colour backtracking fixing colours at one vertex yields precisely the same 20. Two independently formulated exhaustive adjacency computations agree on every one of the 27 edges. A displayed bijection maps all 24 edges of the 16-state component exactly onto GP(8,3); the other four states have precisely the claw edges. Connected-component profiles, all-pairs distances and cycle lengths are checked by the included standalone verifier. The claim is finite, with no inference from sampled cases.

value.rationale: For a canonical 16-vertex cubic symmetric nonplanar graph, the minimum-palette colouring state space literally reproduces the base graph as one connected component, while four other states form a dissimilar star. The full twenty-state exchange graph and the three distinct cycle-profile types answer a natural structural reconfiguration question beyond already studied scalar class counts, and provide a concrete finite benchmark for the general Kempe-equivalence-graph theory.
